time.desc: The leader of one party issued a time-limited ultimatum to his opponent through social platforms on the opening of key sea lanes and threatened to attack its energy infrastructure.
The opponent's military force issued a statement stating that if the opponent implements the threat to attack energy facilities, it will retaliate by completely closing key sea lanes.

One party announced that it had opened dialogue and temporarily suspended attacks on its opponent's energy facilities to leave a window for diplomatic contacts. Officials from the opponent confirmed that negotiations were ongoing.
One party formally submits a ceasefire/end-of-conflict plan containing multiple clauses to its opponent to push for a breakdown in negotiations.
The opponent completed and submitted a formal response to the above-mentioned ceasefire plan, and the negotiations entered a new stage.
The two parties carried out joint military attacks on rival ports/terminals close to key sea lanes and caused casualties.
The two countries outside the region jointly proposed another multi-point plan for a ceasefire and the restoration of normal traffic in key sea lanes to promote an end to the war.
The leader of one side issued a nationally televised address, declaring that he would carry out harsher attacks on his opponents in the coming weeks and set a time target for ending the conflict.
The two parties launched joint air strikes on their opponents' important petrochemical industrial parks/energy-related economic zones and caused casualties.

The leader of one party publicly threatened to bomb the opponent's power generation facilities and transportation hubs on a specific date and demanded that it open key sea lanes; the opponent's camp issued a warning to counterattack by blocking another strategic waterway.
One side agreed to suspend bombings and attacks on its opponents and set a ceasefire window of about two weeks.

Allied leaders publicly stated that the ceasefire did not apply to their military operations on another front, triggering disagreements among many parties demanding that the front be included in the ceasefire.
One party announced that it would implement a naval blockade of its opponent's port and specified the launch date, and the action was promoted at the same time as the talks between the two parties.
The military of one party officially launched a naval blockade of the opponent's port and stated that it would not affect the freedom of navigation of non-opponent port ships through key sea lanes.

The leader of one of the parties involved in the war publicly called on all countries to go to the key strait to rush to transport oil, claiming that the opponent had been basically defeated, and related oil prices rose sharply late at night.
Opponents held large-scale commemorations for forty days after the death of the supreme leader. The successor supreme leader said that his country shocked the world during the war.
